column1: # exec-bit-registry.tsv — the REGISTRY of scripts required to carry the
# executable bit (temperloop#1326, epic #1415). Enforced by
# workflows/scripts/validate-exec-bit-registry.sh.
# WHY A REGISTRY, NOT A SHEBANG GLOB. The item's own originating issue
# proposed "a lint that flags a tracked .sh/.py carrying a shebang whose mode
# is not 755, with an opt-out list for sourced libraries." Measured against
# this tree at adoption time, that rule fired on 96 files: ~35 sourced
# libraries (workflows/scripts/lib/, board/lib/, etc.), 58 `test_*` harnesses
# invoked as `bash test_x.sh`, 2 config/allowlist files sourced by other
# scripts, and 15 further scripts invoked exclusively via an explicit
# `bash`/`python3`/`source` — of which exactly ONE was a genuine defect. A
# one-in-96 signal is not a gate: every gate invokes its target scripts as
# `bash <path>` or via a `make` target, so the executable bit is IRRELEVANT
# to CI and matters only for direct `./script` invocation and for a script
# reading as intentionally-executable to a human — the shebang alone cannot
# distinguish those two populations.
# THE SEED SET (deliberately not exhaustive — mirrors check-surface-
# registry.tsv's own "opt-in, grows as surfaces are added" convention,
# temperloop#1476): this repo's own `workflows/scripts/validate-*.sh` family —
# the top-level, human-invocable validator entrypoints named throughout this
# repo's docs as runnable directly (e.g. "Usage: bash <clone>/workflows/
# scripts/install/doctor.sh …" and this file's own siblings' header
# comments). The item's own motivating instance is exactly this family: on
# adoption day, workflows/scripts/validate-check-surface-degenerate-
# coverage.sh had lost its executable bit (an incidental `mode change 100755
# => 100644` in a rebase, invisible to CI because scripts/quality-gates.sh
# invokes it as `bash workflows/scripts/validate-check-surface-degenerate-
# coverage.sh`) while all 15 of its siblings still carried 755. Registering
# the whole family closes exactly that gap and gives the ratchet something
# real to enforce. Widening this registry to other genuinely-intended-
# executable scripts (bin/subcommands/*, hooks, etc. — none of which
# qualify today; see this item's own investigation) is legal future work,
# never required by this gate.
# FORMAT — TAB-separated, two columns:
#   1. PATH     repo-relative path to a tracked script
#   2. REASON   mandatory, non-empty justification for why this script is
#               intentionally directly-executable (never a bare restatement
#               of the path)
# A registered PATH that currently lacks the executable bit FAILS the gate
# (EXEC-BIT-MISSING, naming the file and its actual mode) UNLESS it is also
# named, with a REASON, on the shrink-only workflows/scripts/config/
# exec-bit-grandfather-allowlist.tsv ratchet (temperloop#1326 acceptance
# criterion 2) — so newly-discovered debt can be registered and made VISIBLE
# without having to be fixed in the same PR that discovers it, while an
# already-grandfathered path becoming compliant (or ceasing to be) is
# enforced to keep the allowlist honest (see that file's own header).
